Freedom 250 · Digital money · Crypto overview

The world: how do the other jurisdictions do it?

The International Crypto Map reads 22 jurisdictions on 13 dimensions each, from who has authority to who bears a loss; 191 of the 286 cells are researched, 85 partial and 10 still open. 7 of its 14 issuer records are live under a local license, 15 cross-border routes were reviewed and none is yet a recurring end-to-end corridor in the record, and most systems still finish in an existing bank or central-bank record.

United States: 13 dimensions, 16 clocks, 11 gaps

The United States remains an active but unfinished federal stack, not one comprehensive crypto regime. The post-22 September record is material: the Federal Reserve proposed its GENIUS application and prudential rules; SEC and CFTC staff issued implementation guidance under existing authority; SEC filed an alleged $15 million cross-border crypto-fraud action; The Clearing House selected the technology for a future bank-token network; and Bridge launched OUSD across four public networks. These are different clocks. Proposed rules are not effective rules, staff FAQs are not Commission or statutory permissions, a complaint is not an adjudication, a vendor selection is not network launch, and a live stablecoin does not prove its reserve sufficiency or redemption performance. Incumbent bank, securities and central-bank settlement records remain authoritative within their scopes.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedCongress and the executive define federal statutes and policy; Treasury, FinCEN and OFAC govern financial-crime and sanctions functions; the federal banking agencies govern institution-specific bank and stablecoin capacities; the SEC and CFTC retain object- and activity-specific market authority; the Federal Reserve and Reserve Banks govern account access and central-bank payment services; states retain material licensing, trust, money-transmission and commercial-law roles.Policy, legislation, rulemaking, chartering, licensing, account access, supervision, enforcement and transaction operation are separate federal and state capacities.

Legal objects
researched
researchedThe existing stack separates payment stablecoins, bank deposits including tokenized deposits, securities and security entitlements, digital commodities, derivatives, pooled vehicles, native cryptoassets and nonfungible objects. GENIUS excludes qualifying tokenized deposits from its payment-stablecoin definition and gives permitted payment stablecoins defined treatment without making every digital asset the same legal class.Crypto is a technology and market label, not a single controlling federal legal object.

Permitted activities
partial
partialIssuance, exchange, transfer, custody, brokerage, dealing, payments, derivatives, fund activity and tokenized-security servicing remain governed by the exact object, actor and jurisdiction. Neither supplies one universal permission for all crypto activity.An approval, registration or exclusion for one object or activity cannot be borrowed by another affiliate, product, venue, chain or transaction.

Entry gates
researched
researchedEntry may require an exact federal or state charter, stablecoin-issuer approval, money-transmission or trust authority, securities or commodities registration or scoped exemption, AML and sanctions controls, product or venue approval, and separate Federal Reserve account and service onboarding. The Federal Reserve proposed application procedures for Board-supervised issuers and specified state-qualified issuers; those procedures remain proposals and do not identify an approved applicant. The SEC order, OCC preliminary charter decisions, CFTC prerule review and TCH network plan operate at different gates; none establishes a generally operating firm or comprehensive regime.Application, conditional approval, final approval, consummation, account grant, technical connection and first use are separate gates.

Named operating actors
partial
partialThe existing owners identify the Federal Reserve and Reserve Banks, Treasury, SEC, CFTC, OCC, FDIC, NCUA, FinCEN, OFAC, DTC and DTCC alongside exact issuers, custodians, banks, exchanges, wallets, processors and networks. The September OCC decisions add proposed Agora and Catena trust-bank legal persons at the preliminary conditional charter stage. Bridge Building Inc. is the identified OUSD issuer within the Bridge/Stripe group; BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY have stated reserve roles; Coinbase, Mastercard/BVNK, Stripe and Visa are distribution or integration paths rather than the token debtor. The Clearing House and Quant are future network operator and technology-provider roles, not deposit issuers for each member bank. The deeper Crypto Infrastructure Hub owns the entity and relationship graph.A consumer brand, parent, affiliate, token administrator, reserve custodian, platform operator and legal issuer may be different persons.

Claims and backing
researched
researchedGENIUS payment stablecoins are private issuer liabilities backed by eligible reserve assets and a statutory redemption framework; the Act does not make them federally insured or government-guaranteed dollars. The Federal Reserve's proposed prudential rule would require covered issuers to maintain fair-value reserves at least equal to outstanding issuance at all times, calculate the position daily as of 5 p.m., remediate deficiencies within 24 hours, and meet a proposed two-business-day redemption standard. A tokenized bank deposit remains a bank-deposit claim. A DTC token is a controlled representation inside DTC's entitlement architecture rather than native bearer title to the underlying security. OUSD is a Bridge-issued stablecoin whose launch page names BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY reserve roles; the first promised monthly attestation had not yet been published.Reserve assets, issuer liability, holder priority, deposit insurance, custody and central-bank money are different property and protection layers.
Date: September 30, 2026

Domestic rails
researched
researchedFedwire Funds, FedNow, NSS, ACH, CHIPS, DTC, NSCC and FICC supply distinct money, clearing, securities and collateral functions. FedNow provides 24/7 final central-bank-money settlement under its rules, but no reviewed official record made it a general securities-DVP, CCP-margin, crypto-transfer or stablecoin-redemption rail. DTC token state, authoritative entitlement, clearing and the cash leg can occur on different systems and clocks.Continuous instruction or token state does not prove continuous cash, securities-title, clearing or accounting finality.

Operating state
researched
researchedGENIUS is enacted but delayed-effective, with Federal Reserve prudential and application rules now proposed rather than final. OUSD is technically live on four public networks, but its first monthly attestation and reconciled supply are pending. DTC has completed limited-production tokenization activity; FedNow and incumbent settlement systems are live; the SEC tokenized-securities exemption is temporary and conditional; CFTC AF80 remains at pending prerule review; the Agora and Catena charters remain preliminary conditional approvals; and TCH's On-Chain Money Initiative remains targeted for first-half 2027 availability. CLARITY has not become law and the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve lacks a publicly reconciled operating inventory.Enacted, exemption-issued, prerule-reviewed, preliminary chartered, final-approved, opened, limited production, generally available and publicly reconciled operation are different states.

Scale
partial
partialDTC disclosed July 15 limited-production workflows involving more than 30 firms, while the deeper Hub carries product- and actor-specific issuance, transaction and network metrics. Open Standard reports more than 200 OUSD partners and more than USD1 billion of near-term liquidity commitments, but those are neither outstanding supply nor funded reserves. The existing country synthesis does not yet reconcile a national entity-level census, legal-entity market shares, custody assets, stablecoin circulation by governing issuer or persistent tokenized collateral use.Participant count, token supply, transaction value, custody assets, revenue, market share and systemic exposure are separate measures.

United Kingdom: 13 dimensions, 8 clocks, 5 gaps

The United Kingdom has a live but partial crypto perimeter: money-laundering registration and financial-promotion rules are current, while the broader FSMA activity, custody, prudential, admissions and market-abuse regime remains scheduled for 25 October 2027. The material post-baseline change is that the FCA authorization gateway opened at 09:00 on 30 September 2026 and is scheduled to close at 23:59 on 28 February 2027. Opening accepts applications; it neither authorizes an applicant nor commences the future regime. Existing FSMA firms generally seek a variation of permission, other firms seek authorization, and the saving or runoff treatment depends on timely application and current status. Retail access remains concentrated at a small number of mostly overseas-facing brands, while applicant identity, determinations, legal-entity market share, custody assets, settlement finality and solvency remain unproved.

researched

Japan: 13 dimensions, 10 clocks, 8 gaps

Japan's digital-money record is a layered extension of incumbent legal claims rather than a new sovereign-money successor. The FSA's 30 September On-Chain Finance Forum adds a national roadmap process covering stablecoins, tokenized deposits, wallets, DEX/DeFi, JGBs and possible on-chain use of Bank of Japan current-account money, while a fourth PIP project links future three-megabank stablecoin payments to trade documents. These are coordination and experiment clocks, not production settlement. XRP Asia's 3 October launch adds Tokyo as a regional XRPL community node, but it is separate from the older SBI Ripple Asia joint venture and changes no Japanese licence, product or settlement state. JPYSC remains a live but closed-loop trust-beneficiary claim, and its lending service creates a separate unsecured repayment claim against SBI VC Trade outside customer-asset segregation. DCJPY remains issuing-bank deposit money; retail CBDC and tokenized BOJ reserves remain pilots. BOJ-NET remains the decisive wholesale yen-finality point unless a later legal and technical record proves otherwise.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedThe Diet and Cabinet define the legal perimeter; the FSA supervises cryptoasset, electronic-payment-instrument and banking actors and now convenes the interministerial On-Chain Finance Forum; the BOJ operates central-bank settlement and retail- and wholesale-money experiments; MOF owns sovereign-debt questions and retains a role with the Diet in any future retail-CBDC constitution.Supervision, system operation, pilot work and sovereign issuance authority are different capacities.

Claims and backing
researched
researchedJPYSC is a specified-trust beneficiary claim backed by trust assets and is neither legal tender, a bank deposit nor deposit-insured. The 30 June snapshot disclosed ¥10,008,294,794 issued and ¥10,008,304,794 in the trust's deposit account. When a customer lends JPYSC to SBI VC Trade, that customer instead holds an unsecured consumption-loan repayment claim outside customer-asset segregation. DCJPY is an issuing-bank deposit backed by the bank's balance sheet. A future retail CBDC or tokenized BOJ current-account balance would be a BOJ claim only if legally and operationally issued.Trust segregation, an intermediary loan claim, commercial-bank deposit insurance and a direct central-bank liability are different protections and failure paths.

Correction and loss
researched
researchedBOJ-NET finality limits reversal but does not eliminate later compensation or restitution. Ordinary JPYSC follows trust assets and redemption law with no deposit insurance; lent JPYSC follows SBI VC Trade's consumption-loan obligation and can be lost in its insolvency because the units are outside customer-asset segregation. DCJPY follows the issuing bank's deposit and resolution regime if its stated classification governs; future retail or wholesale CBDC loss and reversal rules remain undecided.Liquidity support, operational continuity, deposit protection, trust segregation, intermediary lending and terminal loss absorption are different mechanisms.

Evidence boundary
researched
researchedThe completed September 14 Japan Monetary Constitution remains the deeper monetary owner. The October recertification adds the forum and roadmap, Coincheck registration, PIP-4, exact JPYSC scale, lending-loss transformation, 43-bank experiment population and BOJ wholesale sandbox. The 3 October XRP Asia delta adds a Tokyo ecosystem-support node while preserving the separate SBI Ripple Asia, provider, permission and settlement records. The October 14 Accounting Transition evidence note separately owns Japan's quarterly common-loan-data workflow and published analytical uses: shared granular evidence can support distinct governed views without establishing blockchain, real-time journals or a common general ledger. Open questions include current reserve composition, open-wallet use, selected cross-bank settlement model, production cross-border reversal, observed digital-claim failure, exact replaced reporting templates and measured burden outcomes.Later product, reserve, rulebook, transaction and failure evidence may change this normalized projection without superseding the deeper owner.

South Korea: 13 dimensions, 12 clocks, 8 gaps

South Korea still had no enacted general public-won stablecoin regime at the cutoff. The material change is more specific: revised VASP entry and AML controls added reporting for transfers of at least KRW 10 million to overseas VASPs or personal wallets; enacted security-token statutes are being implemented for 4 February 2027 while stablecoin-linked payment remains a later phase dependent on pending legislation; and the H1 2026 regulator survey shows sharp declines in holdings, trading, deposits and profit despite a nearly flat eligible-account count. XRP Asia's 3 October launch adds Seoul as a regional XRPL community node and organizational hub activity, but the launch session and adjacent bank panel do not establish an XRP Asia bank partnership, XRPL deployment or XRP route. The Bank of Korea separately documented empirical stablecoin/FX transmission abroad but not the same significant linkage in Korea, and its annual systems report confirms that BOK-Wire+ central-bank money, not a token pilot, remains the final settlement anchor.

Authority
researched
researchedFSC sets financial policy; KoFIU owns VASP notification and AML/CFT controls; FSS supervises and joined the market survey; BOK owns central-bank-money and payment-system responsibilities; the finance ministry owns material FX policy; and KRX and KSD operate securities infrastructure. Security-token Acts are enacted for 4 February 2027, but subordinate rules were only proposed and general public-won-stablecoin legislation remained pending.Policy ownership, VASP notification, a proposed implementing rule, an enacted-but-not-effective statute and operating-system control are distinct forms of authority.

Stress
researched
researchedThe H1 survey measured a maximum virtual-asset decline of 69 percent, large reductions in holdings, trading and deposits, and a 78 percent decline in exchange operating profit. Indonesia: 13 dimensions, 10 clocks, 7 gaps

Indonesia now has a measurable OJK-supervised crypto stack: two exchanges, two clearing/guarantee/settlement institutions, two custodians and 27 licensed dealers at the August supervisory cutoff, serving 22.93 million accounts and IDR 20.52 trillion of July spot transactions. PT Adhyoka Berkah Maju's IDRP rupiah-stablecoin business model passed the OJK sandbox on 11 June, but no reviewed record establishes an issuer licence, public launch, reserves, redemption or lawful payment use. Bank Indonesia still separates crypto trading from legal rupiah payment, while Bank Mandiri, BRI, BNI, BCA and other banks scale conventional QRIS/account-money corridors. Digital Rupiah remains an experimental future central-bank claim, not production money.

Authority
researched
researchedOJK took crypto and digital-financial-asset supervision from Bappebti on 10 January 2025 and now licenses exchanges, clearing/guarantee/settlement institutions, custodians and dealers under POJK 27/2024 as amended by POJK 23/2025. Bank Indonesia retains currency, payment-system, FX, QRIS, BI-FAST/RTGS and Digital Rupiah authority; PPATK and enforcement bodies retain AML and crime-response functions.OJK trading or sandbox authority does not authorize a payment instrument or central-bank liability; BI payment authority does not license a crypto dealer.

European Union: 13 dimensions, 14 clocks, 10 gaps

The European Union is a supranational legal and supervisory layer, while the Eurosystem owns euro central-bank money and national law still controls important authorization, property and insolvency outcomes. MiCA is effective and the maximum grandfathering period ended by 1 July 2026. EBA counted 39 e-money tokens issued under MiCA and zero authorized asset-referenced tokens as of 1 September. SG-FORGE publishes live EUR and USD e-money-token circulation and reserve composition; BBVA Spain operates bitcoin and ether trading and custody. By contrast, the 37-bank Qivalis consortium says its proposed issuer is still awaiting Dutch authorization and does not issue e-money or provide public payment services. EBA and ESMA's late-September MiCA-review submissions are recommendations, not amended law. Pontes launched with onboarded participants, but no first completed transaction was found; Project Agorá used real value in a controlled test but moved ordinary bank deposits through existing core systems rather than launching a common production token.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedThe Parliament and Council legislate, the Commission administers and proposes revisions, EBA and ESMA coordinate and exercise assigned functions, national competent authorities authorize and supervise exact entities, and the ECB and national central banks govern euro central-bank money and TARGET Services. The Commission's MiCA consultation closed on 30 September, while EBA and ESMA submitted review recommendations; none amended MiCA at cutoff.EU legislation, agency advice, national authorization, prudential supervision and Eurosystem settlement authority are separate layers and clocks.
Date: September 30, 2026

SG-FORGE's CoinVertible products are private EMT liabilities, Qivalis is a prospective private EMT, and Pontes settles eligible tokenized-asset transactions in central-bank money without converting securities into money.Euro denomination or token form does not make an issuer liability, bank deposit, security entitlement and ECB liability the same claim.

Singapore: 13 dimensions, 24 clocks, 17 gaps

Singapore uses overlapping activity- and rights-based regimes rather than one crypto licence. The dedicated MAS single-currency-stablecoin framework was still under legislative consultation and had not produced an issuer licence or MAS-regulated-stablecoin label at the cutoff. The bank operating layer is already material: DBS, OCBC and UOB completed live domestic SGD transactions using their own tokenized-deposit obligations with Swift's blockchain ledger matching and netting before final settlement through existing systems; DBS/Citi and UOB/HSBC also completed live cross-border USD and HKD routes. These are commercial-bank liabilities, not MAS money or a common stablecoin. XRP Asia's 3 October public launch adds a Singapore-based regional XRPL builder and community hub, not a payment licence, issuer, bank consortium or settlement system. DBS separately reports material crypto trading and trust inflows, while OCBC has live tokenized securities and a public-chain gold-fund token. The wholesale-CBDC event remains a bounded SGD Testnet transaction, and legal finality remains in the exact designated or conventional settlement system rather than automatically in a blockchain record.

researched
researchedLicensed DPT providers must apply trust, safeguarding and recordkeeping rules to customer assets. Correction and loss
researched
researchedCorrection can involve provider-ledger controls, a compensating blockchain transfer or issuer freeze where technically and legally available, customer-asset trust administration, bank recall and fraud procedures, designated-system finality, police tracing/freezing, confiscation and insolvency distribution. The Finality Act protects qualifying designated-system transfers once final under system rules, while PSA safeguarding creates books and trust structures without eliminating shortfall, custody or insolvency risk.Irreversible technical transfer, legal finality, asset freeze, recovered proceeds and customer restitution are different clocks with different authorities and loss bearers.

Australia: 13 dimensions, 11 clocks, 12 gaps

Australia's existing-law transition reached an enforcement hinge on 30 September: ASIC reported more than 45 digital-asset-related licence applications, but applications are not licences, and firms needing authority that did not satisfy the no-action conditions risk breach from 1 October. The future DAP/TCP regime remains enacted but uncommenced. On 30 September ANZ, BHP, Citi and Swift also completed a live Melbourne-New York USD corporate-treasury transaction using tokenized deposits behind BHP's ordinary ANZ account channel. This is stronger than Project Acacia's bounded research but does not disclose value, final-system records, recurring volume or exceptions. CBA, NAB and Westpac remain at different proof, working-group and product states. RITS Exchange Settlement Account entries remain the production final-money anchor; no clear public-interest case for retail CBDC has been established.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedParliament and Treasury own the statutory framework; ASIC applies corporations, markets and financial-services law and will license DAPs and TCPs; AUSTRAC registers VASPs and enforces AML/CTF duties; APRA supervises prudentially regulated institutions; the RBA and Payments System Board own central-bank settlement and payment-system functions; the ATO applies tax law.Legislation, financial-services licensing, AML registration, prudential supervision, payment-system operation and tax treatment are different capacities.

researched
researchedProject Acacia deliberately tested different money claims: existing ESA balances, a pilot RBA wholesale CBDC, tokenised commercial-bank deposits and stablecoins. Domestic rails
researched
researchedRITS supplies high-value and feeder-system settlement in central-bank money; settlement is final and irrevocable when paying and receiving members' ESAs are simultaneously debited and credited. FSS supports fast retail settlement through the NPP feeder. Project Acacia coordinated bounded tokenised transactions through several settlement models; September consultation asks how RITS and FSS should support future tokenised finance.Token or trade completion does not prove ESA finality, and RITS finality does not settle every upstream title, custody or customer claim.

researched
researchedANZ, BHP, Citi and Swift completed live USD corporate-treasury payments between Melbourne and New York using tokenized deposits while the customer retained its ordinary ANZ account and channel. researched

New Zealand: 13 dimensions, 16 clocks, 8 gaps

New Zealand still has no single bespoke cryptoasset licence or general stablecoin statute, but the FMA's ECDD-specific designation has created a live, conditional legal perimeter for NZDD issued after 11 March 2026. Each NZDD is issued for NZD 1, backed by ECDD as trustee holding NZD in a bare-trust account at a registered bank, and redeemable by an eligible account holder subject to agreed restrictions; the token is declared not to be an FMC Act financial product only while full-backing, monthly publication and annual independent-verification duties are met. That is issuer-specific relief, not bank money, DCS coverage, central-bank money or approval of every NZD stablecoin. The four D-SIBs—ANZ New Zealand, ASB, BNZ and Westpac New Zealand—and Kiwibank remain dominant conventional deposit and payment institutions; the bounded bank-primary pass found no New Zealand-bank stablecoin, transferable deposit token, crypto custody product or production tokenised-settlement route. Australian-parent pilots cannot be attributed to their New Zealand subsidiaries. RBNZ's 28 September strategy folds Digital Cash into payments modernisation but leaves it unissued in Stage 2; ESAS and NZClear remain the production finality anchors.

researched

Permitted activities
researched
researchedCrypto exchanges and wallets may provide value-transfer services; issuers may issue or manage means of payment; tokens with regulated rights may be offered or serviced under the FMC Act; and VASPs may conduct exchange, transfer, custody, broking or token activities subject to applicable registration, fair-dealing, DRS and AML/CFT duties. ECDD may issue post-commencement NZDD within the exact designation conditions. Direct fiat subscription is limited by issuer terms to verified wholesale investors and direct redemption currently carries a stated NZD 100,000 minimum; secondary acquisition through named exchanges does not create the same direct account-holder relationship. Digital Cash work remains research and design, not public issuance.An issuer-specific designation, a secondary-market token holding, a direct redemption entitlement, a registrable financial service, a licensed market service, a protected deposit and admitted settlement activity are different states.

Entry gates
researched
researchedDepending on the activity, gates can include FSPR registration, retail DRS membership, FMC disclosure and governance, a specified FMA or RBNZ licence, DIA-supervised AML/CFT compliance, CARF reporting status, ESAS account approval or NZClear participation. NZDD additionally depends on ECDD maintaining reserve sufficiency and public monthly verification, obtaining annual independent verification, and satisfying account-holder eligibility and compliance terms. The designation switches off during a defined period of non-compliance until remedy. FSPR registration generally involves limited checks and does not itself confer a licence.Application, registration, licence, DRS membership, AML reporting status, prudential authorization, system admission, funding and first transaction must be tracked separately.

Claims and backing
researched
researchedThe NZDD designation requires ECDD to hold NZD at least equal to the underlying currency amount of NZDD in circulation, as trustee on bare trust for holders, in a trust account whose assets are call debt securities issued by registered banks. Eligible account holders may return tokens and require NZD delivery, subject to commercially reasonable restrictions. The designation does not state that the token holder is the registered bank's depositor or that NZDD is DCS protected; only eligible covered deposits receive DCS compensation. Digital Cash would be an RBNZ-issued government-backed NZD liability if approved, while ESAS balances already are central-bank money for approved participants.One-to-one reserve quantity, bare-trust property rights, an issuer-mediated redemption right, the bank's deposit debt, DCS eligibility, central-bank money and market-price stability are separate claims.

Domestic rails
researched
researchedESAS is production RTGS infrastructure, available 23.5 hours each calendar day, with final and irrevocable settlement on simultaneous debit and credit of Exchange Settlement Accounts. Payments NZ clearing systems, SBI/SWIFT and NZClear feed it under separate access rules. NZClear provides real-time DvP model 1 securities settlement; its cash leg settles in ESAS central-bank money and the transaction is final when its last element is recorded.Clearing instruction, exchange ledger, blockchain state, NZClear securities record and ESAS cash finality are distinct records.

Brazil: 13 dimensions, 16 clocks, 14 gaps

Brazil has moved from a framework statute into an operating but transitional authorization regime. Resolutions BCB 519, 520 and 521 took effect on 2 February 2026, creating specialist intermediary, custodian and broker modalities and bringing specified virtual-asset activity into foreign-exchange rules. At the 1 October cutoff, Resolution 588 made transfers to or from self-custodied wallets at or above US$10,000 specifically reportable to Coaf, while Resolution 589 became effective only for its amendment moving the regulated-institution counterparty prohibition to 6 November; its new customer-balance, custody, proof-of-reserves and staking submissions begin 1 January 2027. CVM separately retains the securities-token perimeter. The S1 bank layer is already unevenly operational: Itaú and BTG offer direct crypto trading/custody, BTG markets its own dollar stablecoin and participates in the CSD BR fund-share mirror, Banco do Brasil offers a crypto-exposure fund and joined Caixa in current mortgage-tokenization design, while Caixa, Bradesco and Santander evidence pilots, development or announced-future products rather than a public token-money launch. Nubank is a material non-S1 retail crypto intermediary with on-chain transfers. Drex is not circulating; production finality remains in STR, SPI and Selic records.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedCongress and the Presidency own the statute and decree; CMN supplies policy and prudential instruments; BCB regulates, authorizes and supervises non-security virtual-asset providers and operates STR and SPI; CVM applies securities law by represented rights; Receita owns tax and DeCripto reporting; consumer, police, prosecutors and courts own their distinct remedies.Legislation, regulation, firm authorization, securities classification, tax reporting, system operation, investigation and adjudication are different capacities.

researched
researchedCovered third-party exchange, transfer, custody/control and issuer-offer or sale-related services require the applicable BCB state. Entry gates
researched
researchedNew specialist providers require BCB authorization before operation. Qualifying legacy providers may operate only through the formal transition and authorization process. Existing BCB-regulated institutions face activity-specific communication and waiting rules. Resolution 589 moved the date after which BCB-authorized institutions must not enable virtual-asset operations with non-authorized provider counterparties to 6 November 2026; the amended wording and BCB transition process must be read together rather than treating continuing operation as a final approval. CVM, STR, SPI, Pix, Selic and Drex retain separate legal-person, product, account, technical, liquidity or pilot-participation gates.Communication, legacy eligibility, application, in-process status, final authorization, counterparty cut-off, product permission, system admission, funding and first transaction are separate clocks.

Named operating actors
partial
partialBCB's March 2026 prudential segmentation places BB, Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Caixa, Itaú and Santander in S1. Their verified digital-asset states differ: Itaú offers app-based BTC, ETH and USDC trading with bank custody; BTG offers crypto trading/custody, markets BTG Dol and is the fund manager named in the CSD BR mirror; Banco do Brasil distributes a crypto-exposure fund and, with Caixa and cooperatives, signed the September mortgage-tokenization development agreement; Caixa, Bradesco and Santander have Drex or tokenization pilot/development evidence but no reviewed public token-money launch. Nubank, though not S1, is a material retail intermediary whose current terms cover buy, sell, swap, custody and selected on-chain transfers. A cutoff SPSAV cohort by CNPJ and final/in-process state remains unavailable.S1 membership, brand, conglomerate, Brazilian legal person, bank licence, SPSAV modality, securities-fund exposure, direct virtual-asset custody, stablecoin issuer, Drex pilot node and settlement participant are different roles.

Claims and backing
researched
researchedFor fiat-referenced virtual assets offered by in-country providers, Resolution 520 requires review and disclosure of issuer, fiat or same-sovereign public-debt reserves, custody, audited material and available redemption or reserve-claim mechanisms, and bars algorithmically controlled reserves. These remain private issuer and reserve claims. Drex pilot units are simulated; STR and SPI balances are central-bank money; a tokenised security carries its own underlying legal right. In the CSD BR project, the permissioned XRPL MPT is a complementary representation of selected deposited fund shares, while CSD BR's system remains the official record.Disclosure and reserve eligibility do not prove one-to-one reserves, direct customer title, stress redemption, deposit insurance, legal tender or a sovereign guarantee; an MPT mirror does not displace the named official CSD record.

Domestic rails
researched
researchedSTR is the production RTGS backbone settling in BCB Reserve and Settlement accounts; SPI settles Pix transfers in Conta PI accounts; Selic owns federal-security book entries. STR and SPI settlements are irrevocable and unconditional under their rules. Private provider books and DLT records form a separate operational layer. The CSD BR arrangement adds a permissioned public-XRPL query and audit representation of selected BTG Pactual fund shares while CSD BR retains the official registration, deposit and settlement record. Drex remains a simulated pilot with no end-user participation.Final central-bank-money, Selic or XRPL settlement does not itself settle, validate or reverse a different system's asset record, cash leg, customer entitlement or provider-ledger entry.

Operating state
researched
researchedThe framework law and BCB designation are effective. The detailed provider, custody and FX rules have been effective since 2 February 2026; data reporting began 4 May and DeCripto coverage began for July transactions. On 1 October, the US$10,000 self-custodied-wallet Coaf communication rule became effective and the 6 November counterparty cut-off amendment entered the rulebook. Resolution 589's new balance, custody, proof-of-reserves and staking submissions remain scheduled for 1 January 2027. Bank operating states range from live direct trading/custody at Itaú, BTG and Nubank, through fund exposure at BB, to design agreements and pilots at BB, Caixa, Bradesco and Santander. CSD BR and Ripple report live use of permissioned XRPL MPTs for a selected-fund record mirror; Drex Phase 2 is closed with its report pending.Effective rule, transitional operation, company-reported live use, reproducible operating receipt, application, approval, closed pilot, unpublished result and future prudential compliance are different states.

researched
researchedReceita reports about R$1.58 trillion in declared purchases and sales of principal cryptoassets from August 2019 through December 2025; R$1.13 trillion or 71.7 percent was stablecoins, with stablecoins about 80 percent in 2025 and USDT 88.7 percent of stablecoin value over the full period. Separately, Pix processed almost 80 billion transactions and more than R$35 trillion in 2025 for 148 million individuals and 12.8 million businesses. CSD BR reports more than R$22 trillion in registered assets, but it does not disclose the selected funds or value mirrored to XRPL.Declared gross transaction value is not balances, net capital flow, remittance volume, unique users, provider market share or reserves; Pix scale is not crypto, stablecoin or Drex scale; CSD BR operator scale is not on-chain project volume.

Stress
partial
partialResolution 520 supplies controls aimed at stress: cash and virtual-asset separation, proof-of-reserve methods, independent assurance, position histories, cyber controls, delisting and withdrawal procedures, non-algorithmic reserve requirements and foreign-custody safeguards. Resolution 589 will require verifiable reserve and staking totals in BCB submissions from 1 January 2027. Current Itaú, BTG and Nubank offerings create real custody and intermediary exposure, but product availability and marketing assurances do not establish customer-asset sufficiency under stress. partial
partialResolution 520 assigns scoped provider responsibility for agreed settlement, asset legitimacy, transaction-data security and customer-operation records; requires individualized customer cash accounts and separation of customer virtual assets; and requires custody discontinuity and foreign-insolvency arrangements. BCB says virtual-asset transaction risk remains with the parties. STR/SPI rules protect settled central-bank-money entries, not virtual-asset price, issuer solvency or recovery. Evidence boundary
researched
researchedThis is a fresh primary-source baseline through the 1 October 2026 intraday cutoff. It captures the same-day effectiveness of Resolution 588 and the effective date split in Resolution 589, and adds a legal-person and product-state bank overlay. It records direct crypto services without converting custody into a deposit, a crypto-exposure fund into spot ownership, BTG Dol into central-bank money, a development agreement into a launch, or a Drex pilot into production. It records the CSD BR / Ripple fund-record mirror without creating a cross-border arc, conflating the MPT with the official security record, or inferring XRP or RLUSD settlement. It does not infer final firm authorization from continued operation during transition.Applicant lists, firm decisions, 6 November counterparty enforcement, 2027 supervisory submissions, product balances, reserve attestations, the Drex Phase 2 report and public project receipts may materially change this record.

Argentina: 13 dimensions, 19 clocks, 11 gaps

Argentina has an operating CNV provider regime, fully applicable to the existing registered cohort since 31 December 2025, with five activity categories, minimum capital, custody, segregation, public proof-of-reserve, audit, conduct and reporting duties. CNV Resolution 1165, published on 7 September 2026, adds a compatibility matrix across agents, crowdfunding platforms, PSAVs, markets and clearinghouses without changing the requirements or limitations of each category. This is not a general approval of crypto as money: legal tender and fiat are outside the virtual-asset definition, and the BCRA still says regulated banks may not participate directly or indirectly in offering crypto to customers while payment-account providers may not facilitate unregulated and BCRA-unauthorized digital assets. That barrier explains the major-bank evidence: Galicia's April 2022 crypto launch was superseded by the May 2022 restriction; Banco Nacion says it is building capability for when the framework permits; Santander's Agrotoken lending work reached a pilot but not a verified current launch; and no live direct crypto product was located at BBVA Argentina or Banco Macro. Global-parent products cannot be attributed to the Argentine subsidiaries. The CNV tokenised-securities sandbox remains separate and keeps the authorized traditional security and depositary/holder-of-record chain behind its digital representation. MEP and Transferencias 3.0 are production fiat rails; no current official CBDC issuance or live pilot was located.

researched
researchedCNV Categories 1-5 cover fiat-to-virtual-asset exchange, virtual-asset exchange, transfer, custody/control and specified issuer-offer/sale services. Natural persons may perform only Categories 1 and 2. Mere issuance, self-trading, ordinary merchant receipt, qualifying decentralized protocols without an identifiable provider and self-custody-only wallets are outside the cited PSAV definition; securities and BCRA-regulated activities retain their own perimeters.An exclusion from PSAV registration is not a general exemption from securities, consumer, tax, criminal, FX or other law.

researched
researchedCovered providers must register before operating and identify the exact categories. Foreign providers face local-structure and nexus tests. Minimum net worth is US$150,000 for Categories 1, 2 and 4, US$75,000 for Category 3 and US$35,000 for Category 5, with a specified 50% reduction below US$2.5 million rolling transaction/custody thresholds. AML registration, governance, custody, systems, audit and reporting requirements apply separately.Registration, exact category, BCRA permission, foreign nexus, AML status, technical operation and current compliance are separate gates.

partial

Banco Nacion, Galicia, Santander Argentina, BBVA Argentina and Banco Macro were reviewed as the major-bank layer. Galicia's own 2022 disclosure records a short-lived purchase, sale and custody launch before the BCRA restriction; Banco Nacion's 25 September 2026 statement describes capability-building pending permission; Santander's Agrotoken work reached a pilot; no current direct crypto trading, custody, deposit token or bank-issued stablecoin was verified at those five institutions.Brand, foreign parent, local company, registered category, bank or payment participant, historical launch, pilot, capability build and current operating service are not interchangeable.

South Africa has an operating but layered crypto-service regime: the FSCA licenses covered FAIS advice, intermediary and investment-management services; FIC Item 22 and Directive 9 impose separate AML and travel-rule duties; SARS applies tax and CARF reporting; and SARB and FinSurv retain currency, exchange-control and settlement authority. Crypto is not legal tender or SARB-backed, and a dedicated prudential stablecoin-issuer regime still was not located. The private market is nevertheless operating. BlockTower, not Standard Bank, is the issuer of the live rand stablecoin ZARU; Standard Bank holds bank-deposit reserves and provides securities custody while Sanlam manages the money-market portion. A 31 July agreed-upon-procedures snapshot reported 52.946 million ZARU in circulation, R53.717 million of eligible reserves and 101.46% coverage, but no audit opinion or assurance conclusion. Standard Bank separately reports more than R1 trillion through its Aroko blockchain-enabled conventional cross-border processing rail. Absa markets a current institutional digital-asset custody service using Ripple technology. Nedbank's planned ZAR/USDC conversion, liquidity and daily-net-settlement arrangement remains a conditional phased rollout with no reviewed production receipt. The six current systemically important banks are Absa, Standard Bank, FirstRand, Nedbank, Investec and Capitec; their states range from live custody or reserve-banking to pilots, preparation and bounded negative results. SAMOS remains final central-bank money. Khokha 2 was a proof of concept, retail CBDC is not being implemented immediately, and the August cross-border Crypto Assets Manual remained a proposal after its 30 September comment deadline.

Claims and backing
partial
partialCrypto is not SARB-issued, backed or guaranteed, and no dedicated prudential stablecoin-issuer licence was located. ZARU is a current private issuer structure: Loop South Africa, trading as BlockTower, is the issuer and FSP; Standard Bank holds cash and deposit reserves and provides securities custody; Sanlam Investment Management holds or manages the money-market portion; and Moore performs monthly agreed-upon procedures. The 31 July snapshot reported R23.314 million of cash and bank deposits plus R30.403 million of money-market funds against 52.946 million ZARU. Direct mint and redemption are limited by the whitepaper to verified institutional clients; retail or other holders use authorized partners. The report says Loop is the bank account holder and fund investor, so a token holder has an issuer redemption claim rather than a bank deposit in their own name. Khokha 2 wCBDC and bank tokens were experimental liabilities inside a proof of concept.FSP authorization, asset custody, issuer debt, reserve account title, reserve-asset custody, direct redemption, agreed-upon procedures, deposit insurance and sovereign guarantee are distinct claims; the AUP report is not an audit or assurance opinion.

Nigeria: 13 dimensions, 18 clocks, 12 gaps

Nigeria has an enacted SEC capital-market perimeter, a July 2026 inter-agency coordination order, controlled VASP banking access, conditional SEC incubation and an applications-open CBN stablecoin sandbox. These are different states. The eNaira is operating legal-tender central-bank money and Access Bank currently provides a bank-account funding and withdrawal gateway to the CBN wallet. cNGN is a separate private claim issued by WrappedCBDC: SEC re-admitted the company to ARIP on 2 July 2026 under conditional approval-in-principle after the displayed 2024-25 test period ended. Its terms promise 1:1 naira mint and burn, deny government backing and deposit insurance, and treat retail holders as non-customers who depend on merchant or exchange channels. The exact reserve banks, current reserve report, direct institutional claims and insolvency treatment remain unproved. The May 2026 IMF report reproduced an issuer-origin estimate of about 66 million cNGN held by roughly 20 addresses, showing real but nascent scale. CBN's December 2024 stability report identified five D-SIBs without naming them; the last reviewed named official list is older, so this wave does not pretend the current five are known. Major-bank evidence is strongest for Access Bank's eNaira integration and conventional PAPSS route; no direct bank-issued stablecoin, crypto trading or custody product was verified at Access, FirstBank, UBA, Zenith or GTBank. RTGS supplies final central-bank settlement; NIP gives fast customer value before deferred net settlement. The CBN stablecoin sandbox remains applications-open and no bilateral crypto route is proved.

Authority
researched
researchedThe Presidency and July 2026 Virtual Asset Council coordinate policy without replacing mandates. SEC owns virtual and digital assets within investment and securities business; CBN owns naira, banks, payments, settlement, eNaira and the announced non-security payment and stablecoin perimeter; NRS owns tax; NFIU and law enforcement own their financial-intelligence and enforcement functions; courts and tribunals adjudicate.Coordination, classification, statutory jurisdiction, entity registration, payment authority, tax administration, enforcement and adjudication remain separate capacities.

Claims and backing
partial
partialeNaira is direct CBN liability and legal tender. cNGN is a private WrappedCBDC liability under conditional SEC ARIP AIP. Current issuer terms promise minting only against naira deposits and one-to-one redemption after token burn for verified users, but say retail holders are not WrappedCBDC customers and the token is neither government-backed nor deposit-insured. The issuer says reserves sit in approved commercial banks but does not name the exact account banks or publish a cutoff reserve report on the reviewed surface. An IMF report reproduced about 66 million cNGN across roughly 20 addresses from an issuer-origin source. No reviewed final instrument established a general private-stablecoin issuer licence joining reserve composition, segregated custody, attestation, direct holder claim, run management and insolvency. Sandbox application requirements test such controls but do not certify an issuer or coin.CBDC sovereign liability, bank deposit, issuer AIP, private stablecoin backing, reserve account title, merchant redemption, retail holder liquidity, custody and deposit insurance are different claims.

Domestic rails
researched
researchedCBN RTGS is the final-money rail: the sending bank is debited and receiving bank credited in a final and irrevocable entry. NIP supplies instant beneficiary value but settles interbank obligations on a deferred-net basis. eNaira is a separate operating CBDC ledger; Access Bank's current app moves funds between a customer bank account and the CBN wallet but does not turn the eNaira into an Access deposit. cNGN uses a private issuer ledger and public blockchain records; designated VASP naira accounts and platform books add further records.User-visible speed, bank credit, deferred net obligation, central-bank finality, eNaira transfer, exchange execution, chain confirmation and customer title are not interchangeable.

Correction and loss
partial
partialCorrection can involve a bank or NIP dispute record, eNaira ledger, designated VASP account, provider ledger, custody or key control, blockchain entry, SEC or CBN action, freeze or seizure, and court or tribunal disposition. cNGN terms warn that blockchain broadcasts are usually irreversible, require the merchant to send to the issuer's redemption address and assign address-error loss to the user; only after burn does WrappedCBDC initiate naira return to the designated bank account. Evidence boundary
researched
researchedThe baseline uses enacted statutes and official Presidency, SEC, CBN, NRS, NIBSS and NDIC records, plus bank-authored and issuer-authored product terms. It labels the latest located eNaira scale as June 2024, treats SEC's July AIP release as later than the directory's expired cNGN test period, and distinguishes current rules from proposals, AIPs and applications. cNGN reserve and bank-partner claims are issuer claims unless joined to bank, auditor and account evidence. Current D-SIB reporting provides a five-bank count without names; the older named six-bank roster is not silently promoted as current. Kenya: 13 dimensions, 17 clocks, 10 gaps

Kenya has an enacted VASP Act and final July 2026 regulations. CBK owns wallets, virtual-asset payment processing, stablecoin issuance and separate FX-conversion authorization; CMA owns exchanges, brokers, investment services, offerings and tokenisation. The rules require fully backed, segregated and insolvency-remote stablecoin reserves plus par redemption within two working days, but no cutoff-specific official VASP licence export or named stablecoin issuer was located. The bank overlay is preparatory rather than a proved crypto launch: KCB describes a possible future role as transaction-, trust-account, liquidity, FX and merchant-rail bank for licensed VASPs; Co-operative Bank reports a risk/compliance assessment underway; Stanbic describes a clearer perimeter for possible partnerships, payment rails and custody-related services; and Absa Kenya reports capacity-building for virtual assets inside its custody franchise. Equity, NCBA, I&M and DTB disclose digital-banking, market-research or conventional investment activity, not a locally launched crypto product. KCB did launch a TerraPay/Mobex incoming-remittance connection on 25 September 2026, but its release proves bank-account receipt, not a stablecoin or blockchain leg. KEPSS remains the production final-money rail and licensed mobile money is a separate conventional PSP system. CBK reported 94.35 million registered mobile-money accounts and KSh728.7 billion of agent cash-in/cash-out value in July 2026; these are not unique users or crypto scale. CBDC remains monitored, and no bilateral crypto route is proved.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedNational Treasury owns the policy and regulations and chairs the coordination forum. CBK licenses wallets, virtual-asset payment processors and stablecoin issuers and owns currency, PSPs and KEPSS; CMA licenses exchanges, brokers, investment services, offerings and tokenisation. KRA owns tax; FRC and law-enforcement bodies retain AML and enforcement functions; courts and tribunals adjudicate. The National Treasury and CBK opened a separate draft National Payment System Policy and Bill on 21 September 2026; the policy anticipates implications for PSP licensing and remittance products that integrate tokenised or stablecoin arrangements, but it is a proposal, not current operating authority.Policy, proposed payment-law reform, category-specific licensing, AML registration, tax reporting, PSP authorization, settlement operation, investigation and adjudication are different capacities.

Named operating actors
partial
partialCBK's 10 August 2026 PSP directory names Safaricom PLC, Airtel Money Kenya Limited and other legal persons for conventional payment services; Safaricom is authorized to issue, process, store, send and facilitate mobile-money payments. The November 2025 CBK/CMA notice said no VASP was then licensed. No post-regulations cutoff export joining a VASP legal person to category, conditions and commencement was located. For the bank overlay, CBK's 2025 supervision report defines an eight-bank Large peer group—KCB Bank Kenya, Equity Bank Kenya, Co-operative Bank of Kenya, Absa Bank Kenya, NCBA Bank Kenya, Stanbic Bank Kenya, I&M Bank and Diamond Trust Bank Kenya. Their own current materials prove different preparation states but no locally scoped bank-issued stablecoin, direct retail crypto dealing or production crypto-custody launch: KCB maps a possible future banking-partner role; Co-op has a risk/compliance assessment underway; Stanbic identifies possible partnership, payment-rail and custody implications; Absa Kenya is building virtual-asset custody capacity; NCBA and I&M publish market research; Equity and DTB disclose digital-banking transformation without a named crypto product.A large-bank designation, PSP licence, strategy statement, compliance assessment, research note, capacity-building programme or parent-group capability is not a Kenyan VASP or stablecoin licence, product launch, reserve mandate, customer custody balance or recurring transaction.

partial

Domestic rails
researched
researchedKEPSS is CBK's production RTGS and its rules make accepted settlement final and irrevocable. Licensed mobile-money providers and other PSPs supply conventional retail payment records. The 21 September draft NPS reform seeks wider interoperability and expressly anticipates stablecoin- or token-integrated payment products, but it does not make a virtual-asset book final central-bank money. VASP books, custodial wallets, stablecoin ledgers and public blockchains remain separate records from KEPSS settlement.A draft interoperability policy, customer-visible speed, mobile-money value, bank credit, VASP execution, chain confirmation, stablecoin redemption and final central-bank settlement are not interchangeable.

Ghana: 13 dimensions, 18 clocks, 11 gaps

Ghana has enacted Act 1154, but full operationalisation remains in progress. Bank of Ghana and SEC divide VASP supervision, FIC retains AML functions, and the SEC names 20 legal persons in a controlled virtual-asset sandbox. Sandbox participation is expressly not a full licence; Bank of Ghana's application and fee pages remained unavailable after their stated end-Q3 2026 target, while the Governor described full operationalisation as a 2027 objective. The latest official virtual-asset risk assessment documents the pre-licensing bank stance: banks and PSPs were directed not to facilitate crypto transactions, filed suspicious-transaction reports, flagged or closed crypto-linked accounts, and referred some cases onward. That is observed control activity, not a current bank-by-bank product census or proof that every bank follows an identical policy. An asset-based review of Ecobank Ghana, GCB, Stanbic Ghana, Absa Ghana, Fidelity Bank and Zenith Bank found no locally scoped stablecoin issuance, crypto custody, exchange link, tokenised deposit or direct crypto dealing product. GCB's G-Money is conventional e-money; Fidelity's eCedi role was a completed pilot; Stanbic's crypto article is thought leadership; Absa's live custody offering names conventional assets. GoldBod's bank financing is conventional and its gold tokenisation is planned for 2027, while Ghana Gold Board and Africoin Ghana remain sandbox actors. Stablecoin issuance is regulated but no complete reserve or redemption regime was established. GIS supplies final central-bank settlement; GIP and mobile money are conventional retail rails. eCedi remains concluded pilot and continuing design, not production. No bilateral crypto route is proved.

researched
researchedParliament and the Minister responsible for Finance own law and policy. Bank of Ghana owns currency, banking, payments, GIS and its VASP categories; SEC owns capital-market virtual-asset services and the sandbox; FIC owns financial-intelligence and AML/CFT/CPF functions; GRA owns tax; courts and tribunals adjudicate. The Virtual Assets Coordinating Committee coordinates without replacing these mandates.Coordination, legislation, category supervision, sandbox permission, AML status, tax administration, payment operation and adjudication are different capacities.

Hong Kong: 13 dimensions, 23 clocks, 11 gaps

Hong Kong has two separate live digital-asset licensing regimes: SFC licensing for centralised virtual-asset trading platforms and HKMA licensing for specified fiat-referenced stablecoin issuers. The official lists still establish 13 licensed VATP operators and two stablecoin issuers, but the issuer operating states have diverged. Anchorpoint Financial Limited's HKDAP entered institutional Beta Access on 12 August, completed a first trade-finance transaction and enterprise B2B settlement workflows, and at 23 September reported HK$1,006,890 in circulation against HK$2,110,045 of unaudited reserves, including HK$1.1 million of issuer-funded overcollateralisation. Independent attestations remain deferred to Full Launch. Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) is Anchorpoint's parent and largest shareholder, reserve manager, reserve custodian and first bank distributor; it separately operates tokenised deposits and institutional crypto custody. HSBC's FRS02 RedCoin remains advertised for a future 2026 launch, although HSBC already operates corporate tokenised deposits, retail Gold Token and Orion digital-bond infrastructure. The five current D-SIBs—HSBC, BOCHK, Standard Chartered Hong Kong, Hang Seng and ICBC Asia—occupy different issuance, custody, tokenisation, CBDC and conventional roles. On 29 September the Government priced about HK$20 billion of digital green bonds, with the HKD tranche incorporating tokenised-deposit settlement through EnsembleTX for the first time; that is a transaction receipt, not general 24/7 central-bank-money operation. The 16 September Policy Address targets tokenised central-bank-money settlement and 24/7 EnsembleTX operation around year-end. e-HKD remains wholesale development, not general retail issuance. HKD CHATS and FPS retain statutory finality for conventional money, and no complete recurring bilateral crypto corridor is proved.

Claims and backing
researched
researchedA specified-stablecoin holder has a par-redemption right, ordinarily within one business day after a valid request. Reserve assets must support outstanding obligations, be segregated and protected through effective trust arrangements; insolvency rights include pro-rata reserve-pool disposal and a shortfall claim against the issuer. HKDAP's whitepaper identifies Anchorpoint as debtor, Ethereum as its initial chain, Standard Chartered Hong Kong as reserve manager and intended custodian, Standard Chartered Trustee as trustee for non-digital reserve assets, and a wholesale authorised-distributor model. At 23 September Anchorpoint's weekly unaudited statement reported HK$1,006,890 in circulation and HK$2,110,045 of reserves, of which HK$1.1 million was issuer-funded overcollateralisation. Independent attestations had not begun. HSBC says RedCoin will be fully backed by segregated liquid assets and redeemable one-for-one, but the product remained future-tense.A statutory claim, whitepaper, unaudited issuer statement and supervisory rule do not prove continuous reserve sufficiency, an independent attestation, liquidity under stress or a completed redemption; issuer equity-funded overcollateralisation is not additional circulating customer money.

HKDAP's issuer dashboard at 23 September reported HK$1,006,890 in circulation, HK$2,110,045 in reserves, 95,010 of transaction volume, and 510,086 issued versus 66,061 redeemed over the preceding 30 days; the figures are issuer-reported and unaudited. The fourth government digital green bond was priced at about HK$20 billion across four currencies, but only its HKD primary-issuance process incorporated tokenised deposits. HSBC reported more than US$1 billion of Gold Token traded value by its 2025 results presentation and Orion reports over US$8.3 billion of digitally native bonds enabled globally. Official monthly data total 867,964,657 HKD FPS transactions worth about HK$8.62 trillion in 2025. No complete administrative series establishes VATP customers or volume, all stablecoin redemptions, EnsembleTX throughput or e-HKD adoption.Licence and participant counts are not users or balances; issuer-reported beta metrics are not audited continuous solvency; whole-bond notional is not tokenised-deposit value; product and platform scale are not national crypto totals; conventional FPS scale is not crypto or tokenised-money scale.

China: 13 dimensions, 14 clocks, 9 gaps

Mainland China does not operate a general licensed crypto market. The February 2026 eight-agency notice, which expressly repealed the 2021 notice, prohibits core virtual-currency business and unapproved RWA tokenization while preserving only exact authority-approved activity on specified financial infrastructure and imposing outbound controls. The separate e-CNY system moved to a 2.0 liability model on 1 January 2026: commercial-bank wallet balances are liabilities of the operating bank with interest, reserve treatment and deposit insurance, while nonbank wallet balances are provider liabilities backed by 100% guarantee funds; PBOC retains top-layer rules and infrastructure. The six large state-owned banks are both domestic systemically important banks and original operating institutions, but their customer and route evidence differs: CCB reports 30.05 million active personal wallets, 2.61 million active corporate wallets and 930,000 active merchants for 2025; PSBC reported more than 33 million wallets by mid-2025; ICBC, BOC, CCB, BoCom and PSBC disclose distinct smart-contract or cross-border receipts. BOC's July 2026 first-batch Singapore CBETS retail transactions correct the earlier signature-only state, but do not supply a complete payer-to-beneficiary finality chain. Private crypto remains prohibited. No route arc is authorized.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedThe NPC and State Council own primary law and administrative regulation. PBOC governs money, e-CNY top-layer infrastructure, payment systems and AML; NDRC owns mining controls; CSRC, NFRA and SAFE own securities/RWA, prudential/payment and foreign-exchange capacities within their remits; public-security, procuratorial and judicial bodies own investigation, adjudication, seizure and recovery. Digital RMB operating centers and bank/nonbank operators perform distinct infrastructure and customer-facing roles.Legislation, policy notice, infrastructure operation, operator approval, payment-system participation, criminal process and a completed transaction are separate capacities.

researched
researchedDomestic fiat/crypto and crypto/crypto conversion, central-counterparty dealing, pricing/intermediation, token issuance and crypto financial products are prohibited, as are financial and payment services for them. Claims and backing
researched
researchedA commercial-bank e-CNY wallet is an account-based liability of that bank, may earn interest, enters its reserve base and receives deposit-equivalent insurance treatment. A nonbank wallet is the provider's liability backed by 100% e-CNY guarantee funds. Deposit insurance currently pays covered principal and interest up to CNY 500,000 per depositor aggregated at one insured institution, with excess claims in liquidation. Private virtual-currency losses may be self-borne when the civil act violates public order, while criminal tracing and restitution remain separate.PBOC governance, bank liability, provider liability, required guarantee funds, deposit insurance, liquidation claim, criminal seizure and actual victim recovery are not interchangeable protections.

researchedThe e-CNY 2.0 framework is effective and e-CNY has material cumulative trial use; official materials still describe trial promotion/development rather than one completed statutory nationwide launch. The virtual-currency/RWA notice is effective. Thirty bank operators are approved but later cohorts may not all be customer-live. The original six large banks have direct current evidence of wallet services, 2.0 interest conversion or application receipts. CIPS and Payment Connect are production bank-money rails. CBETS moved beyond signatures when BOC completed first-batch Singapore customer transactions in July 2026, but public systemwide participant and volume data remain incomplete.Effective framework, trial use, statutory recognition, operator approval, customer service, platform capability, first transaction and recurring production must remain separate.

Scale
partial
partialThrough November 2025, official figures reported 3.48 billion cumulative e-CNY transactions worth CNY 16.7 trillion, 230 million personal wallets and 18.84 million corporate wallets. CCB alone reported 30.05 million active personal wallets, 2.61 million active corporate wallets and 930,000 active merchants for 2025; PSBC reported more than 33 million personal wallets through its app at June 2025, a different measure. mBridge reported 4,047 cross-border payments worth CNY 387.2 billion, with e-CNY at 95.3% of value across currencies. CIPS had 210 direct and 1,619 indirect participants at June 2026 and processed 791,000 transactions worth CNY 19.4 trillion in August. These populations and clocks cannot be added together.Cumulative pre-reform e-CNY use, approved operators, mBridge aggregate, CIPS participants and conventional payment volume are different denominators and do not establish route or active-user scale.

United Arab Emirates: 13 dimensions, 16 clocks, 11 gaps

The UAE has a layered regulatory architecture rather than one crypto licence: CBUAE owns payment tokens, Digital Dirham and licensed financial activities regardless of technology; SCA owns the federal investment-type VASP perimeter; VARA covers Dubai outside DIFC; DFSA covers DIFC; and FSRA covers ADGM. The live CBUAE register still names three Dirham Payment Token Issuance legal persons, while VARA's live register still shows 56 active fully licensed VASPs in its own Dubai perimeter. AE Coin, Zand AED and DDSC have product evidence; DDSC has one disclosed AED 110 million transaction. The major-bank layer is uneven: FAB is a DDSC founding participant and proposed customer-access channel but AEDC Stable Coin LLC is the registered issuer; Emirates NBD's Liv X operates retail crypto brokerage through VARA-licensed Aquanow with Zodia custody; ADCB has VASP risk controls but no verified customer crypto product; and DIB's Crypto.com work remains an exploratory MoU. Digital Dirham has bounded live government and UAE-China CBDC transactions, not proven general public circulation. UAEFTS remains the sovereign RTGS/finality anchor. No map route arc is yet authorized.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedFederal law and Cabinet decisions establish the national frame. CBUAE owns payment-token services, Digital Dirham, technology-neutral licensed-financial-activity jurisdiction and payment-system oversight. SCA owns federal investment-type VAs and VASPs outside financial free zones. VARA covers Dubai outside DIFC, DFSA covers DIFC and FSRA covers ADGM. FTA owns tax; courts, insolvency office-holders and law enforcement own separate adjudication and recovery capacities.Federal, emirate, commercial-free-zone, financial-free-zone, payment-token, investment-product, tax, enforcement and settlement authorities are distinct and may overlap only through an express gate.

Claims and backing
researched
researchedPayment-token holders have a par-redemption right without delay and no later than the same time on the next business day unless CBUAE permits otherwise. The default reserve is 100% same-currency cash in segregated escrow; a bank-owned issuer may hold at least 50% cash and the remainder in short-duration UAE government bonds or CBUAE M-bills. Daily reconciliation/reporting, monthly external audit and an insolvency claim against the reserve are required. Issuer-specific current balances and redemption performance remain open.Statutory design, product statement, dated reserve balance, attestation, liquidity, redemption request, completed payment and insolvency recovery are separate evidence states.

researched
researchedPayment-token, VARA and financial-free-zone regimes are effective; UAEFTS and Aani are production rails. AE Coin and AEDZ present active issuer products. DDSC entered operational deployment in February 2026 and has one disclosed AED 110 million transfer in May. FAB participates in DDSC but the registered issuer is AEDC Stable Coin LLC. ADCB's disclosed VASP framework and blockchain analytics are bank-risk controls, not customer trading or custody. partialCorrection can occur through issuer mint/burn and redemption, agent/custodian/VASP books, chain controls or compensating transfers, bank and payment-system processes, regulatory restrictions, and court or insolvency action. Federal law protects qualifying infrastructure settlement as final and irreversible, while payment-token customers hold a separate reserve-backed contractual claim. No complete loss-allocation and recovery series was found.Technical reversal, ledger correction, token burn, par redemption, licence suspension, fine, reserve claim, confiscation, adjudication and customer restitution have separate clocks.

Switzerland: 13 dimensions, 17 clocks, 10 gaps

Switzerland regulates crypto-related activity through existing functional financial-market perimeters plus the 2021 DLT legislation, not one general crypto licence. FINMA-authorised banks and securities firms, the regulated SIX digital securities infrastructure and the first DLT trading facility supply named institutional entry points. The SNB has issued wholesale CBDC for live production-environment settlement on SIX since December 2023 and extended the bounded Helvetia pilot through at least June 2028; BX Digital separately uses a production SIC RTGS link with traditional central-bank money. All four systemically important banking groups participate in the controlled CHFD stablecoin sandbox, but they do not thereby become issuers: Swiss Stablecoin AG provides issuance infrastructure and CHFD Infrastruktur AG operates the platform. Separately, UBS has live tokenised-securities and fund workflows but no active spot-crypto offer on its cited product page; ZKB directly custodies bitcoin and ether while Crypto Finance executes trades; PostFinance offers 22-asset trading, custody and ETH staking with Sygnum; and no broader Raiffeisen customer crypto product was verified. Stablecoins remain private repayment claims and the sandbox is not a public launch. No permanent CBDC, retail CBDC or recurring cross-border route is established, so the map carries no route arc.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedThe Confederation defines the Swiss franc; the SNB owns central-bank money, SIC rules and payment-system oversight; FINMA owns prudential, conduct and FMI licensing; FINMA-recognised SROs supervise many AML-only financial intermediaries; tax, courts and insolvency authorities retain separate roles. The 2021 DLT Act adapted existing law rather than creating a single crypto regulator.Currency, prudential licence, conduct, AML membership, market-infrastructure approval, tax, adjudication and insolvency distribution are separate authorities and states.

Entry gates
researched
researchedProfessional AML-covered intermediaries require direct supervision or recognised-SRO membership. Current fintech authorisation covers up to CHF 100 million of public deposits or collective cryptobased-asset custody if assets are neither invested nor interest-bearing; larger or invested deposits enter the banking perimeter. Securities, funds and FMIs have distinct gates. Named operating actors
researched
researchedFINMA's current material names UBS, Raiffeisen Group, Zürcher Kantonalbank and PostFinance as systemically important. The authorised-institutions list separately names AMINA Bank AG and Sygnum Bank AG as banks and Crypto Finance AG and Taurus SA as securities firms. All four systemic groups participate in the controlled CHFD sandbox, while customer-product states differ: ZKB provides direct bitcoin/ether custody and an interbank service; PostFinance offers 22-asset trading, custody and ETH staking with Sygnum; UBS operates tokenised-asset workflows but its cited service page says it has no active crypto offering; and no broader Raiffeisen customer crypto launch was verified. SIX operates regulated digital-securities CSD infrastructure; BX Digital is the sole listed DLT trading facility. Nine banks are currently eligible for Helvetia wCBDC, but eligibility does not establish usage by each bank.Legal person, group, ordinary licence, crypto-facing service, product admission, technical connection and active transaction are distinct facts.

Claims and backing
researched
researchedFINMA says stablecoin holders generally hold an at-any-time payment claim against the issuer; classification normally follows public-deposit or collective-investment law depending on whose account and risk the backing is managed for. A bank default guarantee can remove funds from the deposit definition but carries conditions and residual issuer, holder and guarantor risks. The sandbox describes CHFD as 1:1 CHF-linked but does not publish the complete debtor, reserve, guarantee, redemption, attestation or insolvency chain. The participating banks are not automatically co-issuers. Helvetia wCBDC is an SNB liability; commercial deposits and custodied cryptoassets follow different protection paths.Legal design, guarantee, reserve asset, dated balance, attestation, liquidity, redemption request, completed payment, deposit insurance and insolvency recovery are separate evidence states.

researched
researchedSIC is the sovereign Swiss-franc RTGS and finality anchor, operated by SIX Interbank Clearing under SNB rules. SIC instant payments provide 24/7 final account-to-account settlement. Operating state
researched
researchedThe DLT legal framework, SDX/CSD infrastructure, SIC and instant payments are effective and operational. Helvetia wCBDC has been used for live production-environment settlement since December 2023 and now runs through at least June 2028 as a pilot. BX Digital holds an effective licence and the SNB describes its RTGS link as productive. CHFD became technically live inside a controlled sandbox at the end of June 2026 and entered a nine-company use-case test phase on 8 September; the test has restricted participants and limits and is not a public product or market decision. Dedicated stablecoin and crypto-institution licences remain proposed, and no retail or permanent wholesale CBDC is established.Effective law, licence, technical readiness, production connection, bounded pilot, first transaction, recurring operation and permanent policy adoption are not interchangeable.

France: 13 dimensions, 18 clocks, 11 gaps

France implements MiCA through the AMF and ACPR while Banque de France and Eurosystem infrastructure retain the public-money settlement spine. The major-bank layer is already heterogeneous and material: Société Générale-FORGE issues live EURCV and USDCV; Crédit Agricole group company CACEIS Bank issues live EURXT and used it for a first tokenised-fund subscription; BPCE subsidiary Hexarq provides direct retail crypto trading and custody through 13 network banks; BNP Paribas provides indirect BTC/ETH exposure through six ETNs and separately completed a controlled intra-group tokenised-fund experiment; Banque Fédérative du Crédit Mutuel is a Qivalis consortium member while that proposed issuer remains unauthorised; and no comparable production crypto or token-money product was verified for La Banque Postale. These are separate issuer, CASP, securities and development states. On 21 September 2026 the Eurosystem launched Pontes, with Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and Société Générale among the initial onboarded participants, but no France-specific completed Pontes transaction, recurring volume or exception record is yet established. No substantive French legal, licence, product or settlement change was found after 22 September through the intraday cutoff; no route arc is authorised.

Dimension, clock or gapStateWhat the record saysLimitDate, source, links
Authority
researched
researchedThe EU supplies MiCA; French law allocates national powers among the AMF, ACPR and Banque de France. AMF owns French CASP authorisation and conduct, ACPR owns prudential and French EMT-issuer authorisation, Banque de France owns the national central-bank and TARGET layer, and FGDR, courts and insolvency authorities own separate protection and adjudication functions.EU rule, national implementation, prudential licence, market conduct, central-bank operation, guarantee payout and adjudication are separate authorities and states.

Named operating actors
researched
researchedACPR's six-principal-group comparison identifies BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Groupe Crédit Agricole, Groupe BPCE, Groupe Crédit Mutuel and La Banque Postale; the first four were 2024 G-SIBs. Exact operating legal persons differ inside those groups. Société Générale-FORGE issues EURCV and USDCV and is an EMI, investment firm and CASP. CACEIS Bank, the Crédit Agricole asset-servicing bank, is a notified credit-institution CASP and issues EURXT. Hexarq SAS, a BPCE subsidiary, is the licensed retail CASP. BNP Paribas' French commercial bank distributes securities-based crypto exposure while its asset-management, Securities Services and AssetFoundry units performed the tokenised-fund experiment. Banque Fédérative du Crédit Mutuel is a Qivalis member, not the proposed issuer. Circle France remains a separate non-major-bank EMT issuer.Group, issuer, bank, CASP, distributor, transfer agent, tokenisation platform, custodian, CSD, central bank and system operator must remain exact legal persons and roles.
