Claims and backing
researched
researchedEMT holders have at-par private claims on the exact issuer, supported by MiCA safeguarding and recovery/redemption duties. Circle discloses segregated EURC reserves; SG-FORGE discloses segregated collateral for EURCV and USDCV. CACEIS Bank's EURXT white paper makes CACEIS Bank the debtor, permits up to 70% of the reserve in highly liquid instruments and gives identified holders an at-par redemption process. The issuer website's statement that reserves consist entirely of central-bank cash is not fully reconciled with that white-paper permission and the current numerical reserve fields were not machine-readable at cutoff. BNP's ETNs are issuer securities, BPCE/Hexarq holdings are customer cryptoassets and Qivalis remains a future claim. Bank deposits, securities and central-bank money retain separate debtors and protection paths.Issuer disclosure, reserve eligibility, actual reserve composition, central-bank account, custody, attestation, legal redemption right, processed redemption, deposit guarantee and insolvency recovery are separate evidence states.

Domestic rails
researched
researchedT2 settles payment transactions individually in central-bank money with irrevocable and unconditional finality; T2S supplies securities settlement in central-bank money; TIPS supplies instant settlement; ESES France uses simultaneous gross securities transfer and central-bank-money cash settlement. Pontes launched on 21 September 2026 as a DLT-to-TARGET interface, with CDC and Société Générale among the initial onboarded participants. The first EURXT transaction settled a subscription to a Luxembourg-domiciled Amundi tokenised money-market fund on Ethereum, but the reviewed announcement does not establish that its cash leg used TARGET, Pontes or central-bank money.Blockchain transfer and fund subscription do not identify the ultimate cash-finality record; customer interface, token record, transfer-agent record, fund register, CSD entry, participant admission and final central-bank cash remain distinct records and gates.

researched

Correction and loss
researched
researchedFormer DASPs had to enable transfer or sale during orderly cessation. EMTs have issuer redemption and recovery-plan paths. EURXT's contract allows CACEIS Bank to block wallets, freeze tokens, blacklist addresses and recover funds under its compliance controls; those technical powers do not by themselves decide property title, finality or a contested customer's remedy. Eligible bank deposits use the separate FGDR EUR100,000 mechanism; crypto and e-money support are outside it. ETN issuer/custody claims, customer-crypto return, securities compensation, system exceptions, court claims and criminal recovery are separate again.Freeze, recovery, transfer, redemption, safeguarding, guarantee payout, securities claim, compensation, compensating payment and restitution have different operators, triggers and clocks.

Canada: 13 dimensions, 15 clocks, 11 gaps

Canada still uses overlapping AML, retail-payment, securities, banking and payment-system regimes rather than one crypto licence. The post-15 September changes are concrete but narrow: a 16 September multi-jurisdiction decision let Netcoins add Solana to cryptoassets exempt from specified investment limits, and on 22 September all six Canadian D-SIBs announced only an exploration of interbank Canadian-dollar tokenised deposits. No common token, issuer, ledger, customer launch, first transfer, finality rule or production scale was disclosed. BMO separately planned a U.S.-dollar institutional tokenised-cash/deposit platform for H2 2026 pending approval and joined Project Agorá on 29 September; TD disclosed a real-value Agorá transfer, but it was between U.S. legal entities, not a Canadian production route. Q3 Pillar 3 returns show that the banks' present crypto activity is mostly capital-markets intermediation, collateral/repo, brokerage and custody rather than deposit-token issuance: RBC disclosed CAD1.920 billion held under custody but only CAD3 million on-balance-sheet plus CAD28 million off-balance-sheet exposures subject to its simplified-approach deduction, while BMO, CIBC, National Bank, Scotiabank and TD disclosed heterogeneous and often substantially hedged Group 2 books. The Stablecoin Act remains enacted but not in force and expressly targets non-financial issuers; bank-issued tokenised deposits remain prudentially regulated bank liabilities. Lynx remains the production Bank-of-Canada-books final-money anchor, RTR was still scheduled for Q4, and no retail CBDC is issued.

Authority
researched
researchedParliament and the Governor in Council own federal law and commencement; the Bank of Canada owns central-bank money, system oversight, RPAA supervision and the future stablecoin regime; FINTRAC owns AML registration and supervision; provincial and territorial regulators coordinated through CSA own securities and crypto-platform decisions; Payments Canada operates core systems; CDIC, courts and insolvency authorities own separate protection and recovery functions.Enactment, commencement, registration, licensing, supervision, system operation, insurance and adjudication are different capacities.

researched

Finance Canada says the future Stablecoin Act is for non-financial issuers because banks and credit unions already sit inside comprehensive prudential regimes.A tokenised deposit remains a claim on the named deposit-taking bank unless the design creates a different legal object; digital form or a common dollar reference does not merge public money, insured deposit, safeguarded funds, platform contract, stablecoin claim or chain entry.

Claims and backing
researched
researchedCurrent VRCAs remain private risky assets or platform contracts without regulated-deposit protection. A tokenised deposit would be a liability of its issuing bank and is not automatically a common six-bank coin; the announcement disclosed neither deposit-insurance treatment nor a common backing or loss-sharing structure. RPAA safeguarding protects qualifying end-user funds through trust or segregation plus insurance/guarantee. The future Stablecoin Act would require one-for-one qualifying reserves and at-par redemption for covered non-financial issuers but is not in force. USDC remains a claim on its exact issuer.Bank deposit debt, token representation, platform eligibility, reserve rule, safeguard, stablecoin issuer debt, direct redemption, CDIC coverage and actual recovery are separate states.

researched

Scale
partial
partialThe first comparable quarterly OSFI templates expose bank intermediation but not one market-size measure. At 31 July 2026: RBC reported CAD1.920 billion market value under custody, excluded from its capital requirement, alongside CAD3 million on-balance-sheet and CAD28 million off-balance-sheet exposures under the simplified approach; BMO reported Group 2a long CAD11 million, short CAD10 million and CAD7 million capital requirement; TD reported CAD46 million long, CAD23 million short, CAD10 million capital requirement and CAD1 million Group 2b deduction; CIBC reported Group 2a long and short CAD93 million, plus CAD2 million Group 2b and CAD2 million deduction, with CAD378 million assets and CAD212 million liabilities in its CAE2 accounting table; National Bank reported Group 2a RWA CAD150 million, long CAD181 million, short CAD184 million and CAD6 million capital; Scotiabank reported Group 2a long and short CAD35 million and CAD8 million capital, plus accounting balances heavily shaped by crypto-related repo liabilities. These consolidated prudential snapshots differ by method and include hedges, collateral, repo, derivatives, securities and client-broker balances; they do not identify Canadian customers or tokenised-deposit use. The record still lacks national customers, stablecoin circulation, redemptions, payments and corridor volumes.Custody assets, gross longs, shorts, risk-weighted assets, accounting assets/liabilities, deductions and capital requirements are different measures; none alone establishes beneficial ownership, customer geography, payment volume, issuer solvency or corridor scale.

Rwanda: 13 dimensions, 17 clocks, 11 gaps

Rwanda now has an effective virtual-asset statute, but the reviewed official record does not yet show an operational licensing market. Law No. 023/2026 was gazetted and entered into force on 28 May 2026. It makes the Capital Market Authority the primary virtual-asset regulator, preserves a National Bank of Rwanda role over monetary stability and payments, requires licences or issuer approval, prohibits natural persons from carrying on virtual-asset business, treats virtual assets as non-legal-tender, and bars their direct use for payments unless NBR authorizes it. Stablecoins require prior CMA approval, full collateralization, liquid reserves, professional custody, audit and insolvency segregation; algorithmic stablecoins are excluded from the statutory virtual-asset category. Yet CMA's current regulation, application and licensee pages show no implementing virtual-asset regulation, VASP application route, VASP category, stablecoin issuer or approved virtual-asset product. The law is therefore effective while the public entry-and-authorization layer remains unproved. Rwanda's major banks remain conventional deposit, payment, securities-custody and cross-border-banking institutions: Bank of Kigali, BPR, I&M, Equity, Ecobank and Access disclose ordinary digital channels or regional transfers, but no reviewed primary source proves a Rwandan bank-issued stablecoin, tokenized deposit, crypto custody service, VASP licence or real-value token settlement. The e-FRW is still a proof of concept, and the Ghana-Rwanda passporting framework remains permission architecture rather than a transaction receipt.

Legal objects
researched
researchedLaw No. 023/2026 covers transferable or tradable digital value used for payment or investment, real-world tokenized assets and reserve-backed stable-value assets. It excludes digital fiat representations, NBR-regulated payment instruments, capital-market instruments, CBDC, closed-loop value, purely private non-trading value, NFTs, enhanced-anonymity assets and algorithmic stablecoins. The wider record separately preserves FRW cash, NBR settlement balances, bank deposits, e-money, safeguarded PSP funds, securities, covered virtual assets and a possible future e-FRW liability.A statutory virtual asset, excluded algorithmic stablecoin, tokenized security, bank deposit, e-money claim, central-bank balance and CBDC are not interchangeable; exclusion from this law can mean another regime applies, not that the object is approved.

Permitted activities
researched
researchedA CMA-licensed legal entity may provide the services enumerated in Article 14, including issuance/listing/trading platforms, clearing or settlement, fiat or virtual-asset exchange, transfer, order execution, placement, custody or administration, escrow, advice and investment management. Issuance, trading or listing of a virtual asset requires prior CMA approval; stablecoins have additional Article 19 duties. Natural persons may not conduct virtual-asset business. Virtual assets are not legal tender and may not be used directly to pay for goods, services, debts or financial obligations unless NBR authorizes that use. partial
partialArticle 10 requires a legal entity incorporated or registered in Rwanda with local presence, beneficial-owner disclosure, fit governance, regulatory capital and AML controls; regulations must prescribe procedures and capital. Claims and backing
researched
researchedArticle 19 requires an approved stablecoin to be 100% collateralized at all times, bars lending reserve assets for yield, requires independent-auditor confirmation of liquidity for reasonable and timely redemption, verification means, a licensed professional custodian, regular audits and segregation from issuer and creditor assets for insolvency. researched
researchedLaw No. 023/2026 is effective, but the public implementation layer remains incomplete or unproved: no virtual-asset regulation, application route, VASP licence, stablecoin issuer approval, bank token product or transaction appears in the reviewed CMA/NBR pages. partial
partialFIC's assessment records high virtual-asset financial-crime risk and unregulated access. Correction and loss
partial
partialThe virtual-asset law allows a competent authority to order freezes for substantiated suspected illegality, sanctions or investigations; requires VASPs to safeguard customer assets, preserve originator and beneficiary records, screen addresses and report fraud, theft, complaints and remediation; and places unauthorized business, issuance, marketing, payments, mining facilities, ATMs and mixers under criminal penalties. Stablecoin reserves must be insolvency-segregated. Separately, payment-law safeguards, bank-resolution powers and the DGF protect different conventional claims. The global layer: Swift, BIS Agorá, Open USD, The Clearing House and others (6 records)

· 6 rows

Swift says most of seventeen first-mover banks have used its ledger for controlled 24/7 tokenized-value payments in five currencies across six continents; exact bank pairs, values, final-settlement systems and exception records remain undisclosed. Project Agora completed thirty real-value transactions across seventeen controlled scenarios and six currencies, but remains a prototype with manual controls and without standing production integration. Open USD launched on four public networks on 30 September 2026 with Bridge identified as issuer and more than 200 partners; the first monthly attestation, reconciled supply, reserve-account ownership and stress-redemption record remain outstanding. The Clearing House selected Quant for its future tokenized-deposit network, expected in the first half of 2027; vendor selection and legacy-network scale are not launch or transaction evidence. No post-22 September FATF, FSB or Basel instrument was found that itself changes domestic law, firm permission or settlement finality. XRP Asia launched a Singapore-based regional XRPL builder hub with visible Singapore, Tokyo and Seoul community nodes and public intake. The organizational launch changes no country licence, monetary claim, bank settlement or bilateral-route state and authorizes no map arc.

Stablecoin laws, jurisdiction by jurisdiction (9 cards, as of July 28, 2026)

· 9 rows

One home for the Stablecoin Field Guide's law comparison: nine jurisdiction cards (EU, UAE, United States, Hong Kong, United Kingdom, South Korea, Japan x3) kept in the page's own words, each with the page's status line, date, category, lead, 'careful' caution, the compared fields (when, currency, who may issue, what has to back it, who may sell or hold it, how it settles, at the store checkout, currency angle) and the page's links. The chapter's own question, lede and finding are kept in chapter. No existing master covered laws outside the GENIUS Act (stablecoins.json carries only GENIUS provisions), so this file was created; the U.S. card overlaps stablecoins.json#/law_context in subject but not in wording. Evidence is as of the page's 2026-07-28 cutoff. Card src links are the page's links and have not been re-checked against the primary-source rule.

Home: masters/stablecoin_laws.json › cards · 9 rows

LawStatusIn shortWho may issueWhat has to back itWho may sell or hold itHow it settlesBe carefulDate, source, links
European Union: stablecoins need a license as e-money or asset-backed tokens
in forceEurope regulates by legal type of token. It is the clearest category-first model.Only a credit institution or an electronic-money institution may issue an e-money token. Issuers of asset-referenced tokens need a separate authorization.Duties on reserves, liquidity, keeping assets separate, custody and redemption at any time differ by token type. E-money token holders can redeem at face value. Paying interest on them is prohibited.Crypto-asset service providers need an EU-wide authorization and follow EU-wide conduct rules.The token may move on a blockchain. Issuer redemption and bank or central-bank money settle separately, each final at its own time.MiCA authorization is not a European Central Bank (ECB) guarantee, deposit insurance, or acceptance by every merchant.
The law's date: June 30, 2024
Home as of: July 28, 2026
Sources: EUR-Lex — Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 · EBA — MiCA regulatory products
Same row on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption? →
United Arab Emirates: stores may accept only licensed dirham tokens
in forceThe UAE shows that legal routing and merchant permission decide stablecoin acceptance, not contactless (NFC) capability.A UAE company may be licensed to issue a Dirham Payment Token; a bank issues through a subsidiary or affiliate. Issuing, converting, holding and transferring foreign tokens each need their own permission.By default, reserves are 100% cash in the same currency, held in a separate escrow account at an unrelated UAE bank. A qualifying bank-owned issuer may hold at least 50% cash and the rest in short UAE government or CBUAE instruments, with extra capital and controls.Issuing, holding and transferring, and converting tokens are separate regulated services.The wallet transfer is the customer's part. Reserve cash and redemption are separate parts, at a commercial bank or, when directed, in central-bank custody.A terminal that supports contactless payment does not meet the rules on token licensing, conversion, custody, merchants or redemption.
The law's date: August 31, 2024
Home as of: July 28, 2026
Sources: CBUAE — Payment Token Services Regulation · CBUAE — reserve assets · CBUAE — issuance and redemption
Same row on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption? →
United States: the GENIUS Act sets who may issue and what they must hold
enacted · not yet generally in effectOf these laws, GENIUS most directly links more stablecoins to more government-debt purchases for reserves. It also shows most clearly that stablecoin law is banking law too.Permitted issuers are subsidiaries of insured depository institutions, federal qualified issuers, or state qualified issuers, divided by the law's federal–state split and size threshold.Reserves must match coins one-to-one: cash, central-bank balances, insured deposits, Treasury bills of 93 days or less, qualifying repurchase agreements (repo), government money funds and related liquid government assets. Issuers report monthly. Holders get no interest and no FDIC insurance.Wallets, card networks, processors and distributors can be separate companies from the legal issuer. A restriction on service providers starts in 2028, setting a later deadline for market access.Blockchain transfer, card-network obligation, minting and redemption, bank-deposit movement and central-bank final settlement stay separate.Enacted does not mean in effect. A proposal, a charter application or a conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) is not a live GENIUS issuer authorization.
The law's date: July 18, 2025
Home as of: July 28, 2026
Sources: Congress — Public Law 119-27 · OCC — 2026 proposed issuances · OCC — 2026 final issuances
Same row on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption? →
Hong Kong: issuing a stablecoin requires a license from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority
in forceHong Kong uses licensing by the regulator: a strict issuer license in an international financial center.Issuing an in-scope stablecoin tied to a government currency (fiat-referenced) in Hong Kong requires a license. So do specified issuing or offering activities linked to Hong Kong.HKMA supervision focuses on reserve management, redemption, risk management, governance, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing (AML/CFT) controls, and disclosure.Only specified regulated institutions may offer in-scope stablecoins to retail investors. The issuer's license and the permission to distribute are separate.The Ordinance covers the issuer and the token's promise, not the merchant's card processor (acquirer) or the final bank-money payment.A sandbox place, a license application or a public announcement is not a license.
The law's date: August 1, 2025
Home as of: July 28, 2026
Sources: HKMA — stablecoin issuer framework · HKMA — supervision guideline
Same row on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption? →
United Kingdom: issuing stablecoins becomes a licensed activity; the full regime is expected to start in late 2027
law made · regime scheduledBritain is the best example of a license requirement already in law whose operating rules are still being written.Issuing a UK qualifying stablecoin becomes a regulated activity. For systemic payment stablecoins, the Bank of England adds oversight to FCA supervision.Qualifying stablecoins are tied to a government currency and hold backing assets. Detailed FCA rules are expected to provide full backing and redemption rights.Safeguarding and other crypto activities need separate permissions. The government is still settling what the dealing and payment-services rules cover.The UK is explicitly designing stablecoins as both cryptoassets and possible payment instruments, with separate oversight of systemic ones.Do not call the late-2027 regime live. Current policy notes explicitly describe more rules and payments reform still to come.
The law's date: 2026-02
Home as of: July 28, 2026
Sources: HM Treasury — cryptoasset regime · HM Treasury — April 2026 stablecoin payments note · HMRC — stablecoin tax treatment
Same row on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption? →
South Korea: a bank-led won stablecoin is under discussion, not law
under policy discussion · not enactedKorea is the comparison case: strong technical readiness does not mean settled law.A bank-centered model, including a debated consortium with banks holding 50%+1, was discussed, not adopted.Not final.Not final. Existing bank-token and wholesale-settlement pilots are separate from any won-stablecoin law.The Bank of Korea's work puts central-bank and commercial-bank money first, with stablecoins as a supplementary option.A committee discussion or a bank proof of concept is not a won-stablecoin law.
The law's date: March 4, 2026

Japan: trust-issued stablecoins may hold up to half their reserves in short government bonds
in forceLike GENIUS, Japan lets reserves fund government debt, but more narrowly: only trust stablecoins may hold limited short government bonds.Banks, registered funds-transfer providers, and trust companies or trust banks issue different legal claims. A lighter intermediary that holds no customer assets may broker for a full provider.Covered trust stablecoins may hold up to 50% in qualifying government bonds of three months or less, or in term deposits that can be withdrawn early without losing principal. At least 50% stays in demand deposits. Rules on daily fair-value measurement and fixing shortfalls apply.Full EPI providers handle sale, exchange, brokering or custody. The lighter intermediary cannot hold customer assets.Trust redemption, deposit-token settlement, bank reserves and a public-blockchain transfer are different things. Each settles on its own timeline.JPYSC running on controlled venues is not open-wallet circulation at merchants. Tokenized bank deposits are not trust stablecoins.
The law's date: June 1, 2026
Home as of: July 28, 2026
Sources: FSA — final implementing package, 22 May 2026 · FSA — 2025 bill overview · FSA — stablecoin Q&A
Same row on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption? →
Japan: crypto trading moves under securities law; stablecoins stay under payments law
enacted · not yet in effectThe split is the key point. Japan keeps ‘crypto,’ ‘stablecoin’ and ‘bank deposit’ as separate legal things.This is not a new stablecoin issuer category. Stablecoins, as electronic payment instruments, stay under the PSA.This card covers no change to stablecoin reserves.Rules on trading, offerings, lending, management, advice, disclosure, intermediary duties and unfair trading move under the FIEA.The law deliberately keeps market regulation separate from the settlement of payment money.Do not say Japan made every cryptoasset a security, legal tender or a bank deposit.
The law's date: July 15, 2026
Home as of: July 28, 2026
Sources: FSA — Diet bills · FSA — 2026 reform overview
Same row on: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption? →
Japan: paper checks and bills to stop clearing from April 2027 (a plan, not a stablecoin law)
official transition plan from industry and governmentJapan is changing both ends at once. It is retiring paper claims while making new tokenized claims legal.Banks still owe the payment; only the form of the payment instruction changes.No stablecoin reserve rule applies.Electronically recorded monetary claims and internet transfers replace presenting paper.This is a direct move from cash and checks to electronic payment systems, separate from stablecoin law.This is an official transition plan. It is not a stablecoin law, and it does not prove every check disappears on one day.
